dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Lauma, we're here to visit!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, boxes piled up everywhere, some of them opened up, loose items strewn all over the floor... Isn't this supposed to be a library?

choices.text: Seems more like a storeroom at this point.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look, Lauma's over there talking to a Weasel Thief... What are they plotting this time? Let's go see.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: *sigh* Be that as it may, we don't have any urgent excavation work for you at the moment... So please, stop digging holes all over the place, alright?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: That's a good child. Here, this Mora is for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's the Weasel Thief from last time, right? What was Lauma saying? Have they found another relic?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: #Hello there, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. Welcome to the library. Is there anything I can help you with?

choices.text: I saw you talking to the Weasel Thief.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: No. I was just giving the little one a bit of a stern warning. It's been getting a little overexcited lately, and it's starting to bother the community.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Its passion for treasure-hunting has only grown since we retrieved the Lunar Semblance... It comes to me all the time, asking when the next treasure hunt will be.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I keep repeating that we now have more than enough documents and relics in our library to occupy our research, but alas...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Yes. But it doesn't quite understand what constitutes a "relic," so it simply digs up anything that seems valuable and drops it off here.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: It has at least promised me that it won't go digging around again, but there's already a big backlog of items from previous digs... There's no way around it. I'll just have to go through and sort them one by one.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Sorry, you two. I'm afraid I won't be able to accompany you on your sightseeing today.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Phew... Now then, what's in this box again...?

choices.text: It went off treasure-hunting on its own?
Have you found some more buried relics?
Are they doing some more renovations?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Finally, some progress at last. Now to somehow put all these things back where they belong...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is quite an eclectic mix...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I know... There's petrified seeds of an ancient tree, fossilized animal bones, colorful stones...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Mora deposit boxes that people buried for safekeeping, wish-boxes, letters with photos enclosed...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like it grabbed everything it could get its hands on!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Well, weasel thieves have a different perspective on value from us. It seems like this one just bagged anything and everything that grabbed its attention.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The seeds and rocks will be easy enough to deal with, but those storage boxes and wish-boxes will have been buried with the express purpose of digging them up at a later date.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will you need any help?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Thanks for the kind offer, but I've already engaged another, slightly more mature weasel thief to handle this. It will be in charge of moving all the items back to their original spots.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: After all, the kid's heart was in the right place. Making it put everything back where it found it would break its poor little heart.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But won't the other weasel thief you hired tell the first one everything?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hopefully not. The little one prefers to live on its own and act solo, so they're unlikely to meet.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It also has a short attention span. Give it half a month, and I'd be very surprised if it still remembers anything it dug up.

choices.text: You sure are an expert in animal behavior.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I speak their language, and I've had the privilege of their company for a long time. It's only natural that I've come to understand them — no different from making friends.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: By contrast, other people can't understand what animals are saying, so they're bound to make mistakes when trying to understand them.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: That's why, in a lot of literature on the topic, phrases like "bestial nature" are rife with negative connotations, while "human nature" is seen in a more rounded light...

choices.text: Well, humans are the ones writing the books...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Heh... You're right. I'm sure those books would have turned out quite differently if they were written by a wolf or a rimehorn deer.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: ...In any case, to me, "human nature" and "bestial nature" are both simply "nature."

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Whether human or beast, all have moments of courage and of cowardice, times of both greed and rage...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: We all rejoice in our successes and mourn our failures... These experiences are neither inherently human nor inherently animal. They are a part of our shared nature — a nature bestowed upon all living things by Mother Nature herself.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I do sometimes wonder whether the world around us might have turned out for the better if humans and animals could communicate with each other.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: But I know it is but a fantastical idea that can never be.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Then there are those who reject nature, and turn their back on the natural way.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: They are the wayward ones who do not hesitate to pull the trigger, even when they speak the same language as the object of their slaughter.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: ...Yes, child. I know you can protect yourself, and that you are far fleeter of foot than they. Do not worry, no one shall harm you again.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Ah, how time flies. I should get back to sorting through that pile of treasure.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I should have enough time to get everything in order before the weasel thief arrives.

choices.text: They can't hear the animals' side of the story...
And you understand their psychology, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, look, {NICKNAME}. There's that weasel thief again, and it's standing right next to Lauma.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? It took off...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Has it seen the error of its ways?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #Come here, {NICKNAME}. Our little friend asked me to pass this Mora on to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Eh? Why would a weasel thief give {NICKNAME} its Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: As I said, it greatly admires your treasure-hunting abilities, and wishes to join you in unearthing every treasure chest in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Consider this its "deposit."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wait, so it was serious?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: When Mora is involved, a weasel thief never lies.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Keep it safe. This coin represents an agreement between you and the weasel thieves... or at least, this weasel thief.

choices.text: Digging up treasure's just a side gig for me...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I wouldn't worry. I know I said it's an "agreement," but I believe it just wants to make friends with you.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: It didn't know what kind of gift you'd like, so it chose to give you its favorite thing.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Please do. If you're interested in taking up the offer, leave some Dried Lakkaberries by your pillow when you get home. It's very fond of those.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Not too many, of course. It might struggle to burrow its way home if it eats too much.

choices.text: I'll take good care of it.
I'm not actually a professional in this field...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: There, all better. Next time, if it's too heavy — don't try and lift it.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Acting tough isn't going to solve anything. Now, if you injure yourself again, or if there's an emergency, you know where to find me, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Off you go, now. Oh, actually, one moment...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Take this twig. I picked it up by the roadside. It seems nice and sturdy.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Of course. And do tell your friends that they're always welcome here if they need a warm place to stay — I know the weather's been quite cold lately.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: This book belongs... here, I think. Huh, there's one missing. That's strange...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hmm, claw marks on the shelf. And feathers...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I bet one of the puffins took it to use as a cushion again. Ah, those little rascals...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I need you to head back into the woods and see if anyone has a book in their nest.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: If you find it, please bring it back. And tell whoever took it that they can come to me if they'd like a cushion to sit on.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Phew... We need to make some more cushions... I think we're going to need everyone's help.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Phew... Now then, what's in this box again...?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: What do we have here...? Ah, that goes in this pile...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: If you're interested in taking up the offer, leave some Dried Lakkaberries by your pillow when you get home. It's very fond of those.
